elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 7(a): "EACH PARTY'S MAXIMUM AGGREGATE LIABILITY TO THE OTHER ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO..." — replaces the split one-sided formulation in the original.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap is "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and "paid" only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 7(b): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" includes "ITS BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS", and the cap opens "EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims definition lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out.
"EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS...", sitting outside the cap.
Excluded Claims include "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILFUL MISCONDUCT".
Excluded Claims include "GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILFUL MISCONDUCT".
Fraud does not appear anywhere in the Excluded Claims definition or elsewhere in Section 7.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the rendered Excluded Claims definition; the prior "PARAGRAPH 9" exception was deleted and not replaced with an IP carve-out.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered 7(a) states that Company's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; the mutual cap on its face could be read to cap Company's payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "EACH PARTY'S MAXIMUM AGGREGATE LIABILITY TO THE OTHER ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO..." — single mutual cap replacing the asymmetric Contractor/Company sentences.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — replaces the per-SOW fees basis.
Excluded Claims (outside the cap) expressly include "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include "ITS BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS"; Section 8 confidentiality liability now sits outside the cap.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the cap is mutual, based on fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, and indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are lifted out via a defined Excluded Claims term.

Preferred level is not reached: (i) no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and the basis is 'fees paid' rather than 'fees paid or payable'; (ii) no data protection/security carve-out; (iii) no fraud carve-out; (iv) no carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP; (v) no statement that Company's payment obligations are not 'damages' subject to the cap. To reach preferred, add the floor and 'paid or payable', and extend Excluded Claims to data protection/security breach, fraud and IP infringement, plus a sentence that Company's obligation to pay fees due is not subject to the cap.

Claimed finding status 'deviation' is correct on the original: the Contractor-side cap was limited to fees paid under the particular Statement of Work (potentially far below twelve months' fees) and the sole exception pointed to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), leaving indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap.

Minimality holds: the edit rewrites only the cap sentence and its carve-out mechanic — both squarely within the selected elements — retains the Statement of Work reference and leaves 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion untouched; no extras (survival tails, procedures, extra damages categories) were added. Caveat for the drafter: if Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) contains a Contractor tax or status indemnity, confirm it is captured by 'INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS' so the deleted exception does not narrow existing Customer-favourable protection.

Intent preserved: the definition of Fees/Services and SOW mechanics are unaffected, the broken/mismatched 'PARAGRAPH 9' cross-reference is cured by a self-contained Excluded Claims definition, and no dangling term or contradictory retained sentence is left.
